questions.claim: Flipping a fair coin 3 times, the chance of exactly two heads is 1/2.

questions.claim: Three doors hide one prize. You pick a door, and the host, who knows where the prize is, opens a different door that has no prize. Switching to the last closed door wins 2 times in 3.
questions.fact: Your first pick is right 1 time in 3. The other 2 times the host's choice leaves the prize behind the last door.
questions.why: Two closed doors feel like 50-50. They are not, because the host's choice carries information.

questions.claim: A disease affects 1 person in 1,000. A test catches 99% of cases and wrongly flags 1% of healthy people. Someone who tests positive has less than a 50% chance of having the disease.

questions.why: A rare condition produces more false alarms than true ones, even from a good test.
